text:
Alex G: Heads up — customer AcmeCorp hitting broken CSV downloads from Console > Analytics > Usage. They see the table in UI but the downloaded CSV is either empty (0 bytes) or truncated after ~65k rows. They attached a sample presigned URL and screenshot.

support-bot: Created INC-3421 for AcmeCorp, priority P2. Asking for repro steps and browser/OS.

Alex G: Repro steps from customer: 1) Open Analytics -> Usage 2) Filter date range 3) Click Export CSV 4) Download/save CSV (Chrome on Win10)
They gave this sanitized presigned URL (shortened): https://s3-presigned.../acme-usage.csv?X-Amz-...

Maya R: Can you run a curl -v against the presigned URL and paste the headers + first 200 bytes? Also need browser console network HAR if possible.

Alex G: Pasting curl output (sanitized):
```
$ curl -v "https://s3-presigned.../acme-usage.csv?X-Amz-..." -o out.csv
*   Trying 52.46.1.2...
* Connected to s3-presigned... (52.46.1.2) port 443 (#0)
> GET /acme-usage.csv?X-Amz-... HTTP/1.1
> Host: s3-presigned...
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< date: Tue, 02 Sep 2025 15:12:01 GMT
< content-type: text/csv; charset=utf-8
< content-encoding: gzip
< accept-ranges: bytes
< last-modified: Tue, 02 Sep 2025 14:59:11 GMT
< x-amz-request-id: 1234ABCD
< x-amz-id-2: ...
< 
* Connection #0 to host s3-presigned... left intact
```
File sizes: S3 console reports object size 12,345,678 bytes, but downloaded out.csv is only 12,344 bytes. Opening out.csv in editor shows header row then lots of NUL (\u0000) padding, then EOF.

Josh P: Weird — headers show content-encoding: gzip but content-length missing in the response. CloudFront sometimes strips Content-Length on chunked/gzip responses; if we have a gzip middleware that calls Flush early we can end up streaming with chunked encoding and the browser might stop reading if the response stream closes unexpectedly. Can you confirm whether the exporter service is setting Content-Length?

Alex G: Asked the customer to try `curl -sSL -D - "URL" -o acme.csv` and open in VSCode — they say VSCode shows full content, Excel shows an empty file or only the header. They also tried right-click Save Link As and sometimes get full file.

Emily S: Customer-facing workaround: Tell them to open in a text editor or use curl/wget to get raw file. Also suggest using Excel "Data > From Text/CSV" instead of double-click — that sometimes handles BOM/encoding. I added this to the INC notes.

Maya R: Alex — can you paste the analytics-exporter logs around the timestamp Tue Sep 02 15:12:01 and the x-amz-request-id (1234ABCD)? We need to see whether we gzip the response ourselves or we hand a pre-compressed object from S3.

Alex G: Log excerpt (sanitized):
```
2025-09-02T15:11:59Z INFO export: start job job_id=exp-9876 org=acme size=12345678 rows=812345
2025-09-02T15:12:00Z INFO export: streaming to response job_id=exp-9876 writer=gzip
2025-09-02T15:12:01Z ERROR export: write error job_id=exp-9876 err=\"write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->52.46.1.2:53242: write: connection reset by peer\"
2025-09-02T15:12:01Z INFO export: finished job job_id=exp-9876 bytes_sent=12344
```
Weird that bytes_sent is tiny and there's a connection reset.

Josh P: Connection reset by peer could be client abort (Excel opening and closing?) but the customer consistently reproduces across machines. Another theory: CloudFront/edge is timing out when we stream a gzipped response without Content-Length. If GC or the middleware calls WriteHeader after starting to Write, the framework might switch to chunked transfer; if some proxy mishandles chunked+gzip we see truncation. Also BOM/encoding could mess with Excel rendering (empty rows), but that wouldn't explain truncated size discrepancy.

Maya R: Agree. Priority: Confirm whether our exporter sets Content-Length for gzipped responses. If not, change to upload final CSV to S3 first and return a presigned S3 GET (with proper Content-Length and content-encoding) instead of streaming through the service. That will also give us reliable retries.

Alex G: I've flagged eng-analytics and eng-infra and set this to P1 for the customer (they're on Dedicated tier). Customer wants ETA/temporary fix.

Emily S: Noted. I'll message the customer with the workaround and let them know we're investigating; offer direct curl instructions (attached).

Maya R: Quick patch plan: 1) Fallback: stop streaming gzipped responses through app layer; write to temp S3 and return presigned URL (short term) 2) Long term: ensure middleware sets Content-Length or avoid premature gzip flush + validate CloudFront config. I'll open a PR and request an expedited canary.

Josh P: I'll check CloudFront behavior and logs for that edge (eu-west-1). If we see truncation patterns there we can roll a config fix.

Alex G: Thanks — adding INC-3421 notes and tagging customer success to offer export workaround. Will post updates here with PR/rollout times. :eyes:
